text:
Leah W.: Hey team — BrightLane just opened a support ticket: sustained 429s hitting their dedicated pool since 09:22 UTC. They see scale up/down every ~30s and request latency spikes. fyi @oncall-eng
Carlos M.: looking
Maya S.: putting the tenant id and logs in the thread
Leah W.: tenant=brightlane-prod-1
Leah W.: quick snippet from access logs:
```
2025-06-05T09:21:58Z tenant=brightlane-prod-1 req=POST /v1/completions status=200 latency_ms=120
2025-06-05T09:22:05Z tenant=brightlane-prod-1 req=POST /v1/completions status=429 latency_ms=5
2025-06-05T09:22:37Z tenant=brightlane-prod-1 req=POST /v1/completions status=200 latency_ms=150
```
Carlos M.: autoscaler logs look noisy — scale decisions toggling between +1 and -1. excerpt:
```
[09:22:04] pool=dedicated-brightlane nodes=2 metric=queue_length=12 decision=scale_up
[09:22:34] pool=dedicated-brightlane nodes=3 metric=util=20% decision=scale_down
[09:23:05] pool=dedicated-brightlane nodes=2 metric=queue_length=15 decision=scale_up
``` 
Maya S.: looks like metric smoothing window is 10s; bursty traffic causes overreaction. Also cooldown currently 20s.
oncall-eng: acked — triaging. Any repro steps from support?
support-bot: Customer reproducer: run 100 concurrent requests with 50ms think time for 60s. They shared a k6 script.
John P.: can we get telemetry: per-node token throughput + queue length over time? infra-bot, can you attach charts?
infra-bot: attaching graphs: cpu_util, avg_latency, inflight_reqs, queue_length for pool dedicated-brightlane between 09:20–09:25 UTC. (see attached)
Leah W.: visible: queue_length spikes align with scale_up events, but util drops quickly once new node added -> scale_down follows.
Carlos M.: hypothesis: aggressive proportional gain + short cooldown => pendulum. Also prefix caching cold-start per node adds short-lived backlog.
Maya S.: suggested mitigation: increase cooldown to 90s and switch smoothing to exponential with tau=30s. Also set min_nodes=3 during peak window.
oncall-eng: can we test a config change in staging? I can roll a codelab to repro the k6 pattern against a staging pool.
John P.: temporary workaround for BrightLane: enable request-rate cap per-tenant @ gateway to flatten bursts. Will coordinate with support to flip it.
Leah W.: customer agreed to try capping at 200rps for 5m. They're OK with slower throughput while we stabilize.
Carlos M.: plan of action:
 - repro in staging with k6 (Maya)
 - try cooldown=90s + smoothing tau=30s (Carlos)
 - enable per-tenant cap for production as temporary (John)
 - observe for 2 hours, then roll back if stable (oncall-eng)
Maya S.: repro notes: k6 script snippet
```
import http from 'k6/http';
export default function() {
  let url = 'https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/completions';
  let payload = JSON.stringify({model:'r-instruct-7b', prompt:'hi'});
  let params = {headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer x'} };
  http.post(url, payload, params);
}
```
oncall-eng: tagging this P1-tier? it's affecting SLA for dedicated customer. escalating to eng-runtime if config change doesn't stabilize in 60m.
support-bot: BrightLane will provide run id and logs after they try the cap.
Leah W.: thanks. I'll update ticket with action items and ETA 09:40 UTC.
Carlos M.: if mitigation fails, next step is hysteresis: require both queue_length and sustained util>60% for 2 consecutive windows before scaling up.
Leah W.: good. keeping this thread for logs. :thumbsup:
